subject: English 1st Paper (English For Today)
topic: Re-arranging Sentences (Question No. 9: ঐতিহাসিক ঘটনা ও নীতিশিক্ষামূলক গল্পের রি-অ্যারেঞ্জ সমাধান)
book: Original practice and user-provided Class 8 Model Tests

items.text:
9. Put the following parts of the story in correct order to make the whole story. Write the corresponding letters in sequence.

(a) He suggested taking it to the nearby police desk.
(b) Mina was walking home from school one afternoon.
(c) There, an officer recorded where Mina had found it.
(d) She picked it up and asked the stallkeeper if he knew its owner.
(e) She thanked Mina for acting honestly.
(f) On her way, she noticed a purse beside a tea stall.
(g) After describing it, she received it from the officer.
(h) Later, a woman came to the desk looking for her missing purse.
items.explanation:
Correct order: b → f → d → a → c → h → g → e

Mina was walking home from school one afternoon. On her way, she noticed a purse beside a tea stall. She picked it up and asked the stallkeeper if he knew its owner. He suggested taking it to the nearby police desk. There, an officer recorded where Mina had found it. Later, a woman came to the desk looking for her missing purse. After describing it, she received it from the officer. She thanked Mina for acting honestly.

9. Put the following parts of the story in correct order to make the whole story. Write the corresponding letters in sequence.

(a) One hot week, he forgot to water it.
(b) Rafi kept a small plant on his balcony.
(c) His sister noticed the problem and told him.
(d) Over the next few days, the leaves slowly became firm again.
(e) He watered the plant and moved it away from the strongest afternoon sun.
(f) Soon its leaves began to droop.
(g) Rafi made a watering reminder so he would not forget.
(h) Rafi checked the soil and found it dry.
items.explanation:
Correct order: b → a → f → c → h → e → d → g

Rafi kept a small plant on his balcony. One hot week, he forgot to water it. Soon its leaves began to droop. His sister noticed the problem and told him. Rafi checked the soil and found it dry. He watered the plant and moved it away from the strongest afternoon sun. Over the next few days, the leaves slowly became firm again. Rafi made a watering reminder so he would not forget.

9. Put the following parts of the story in correct order to make the whole story. Write the corresponding letters in sequence.

(a) Nila filled in the registration form with help from her parent.
(b) At the desk, the librarian explained that she needed a library card.
(c) Nila wanted to borrow a storybook from the town library.
(d) A week later, she returned it on time.
(e) The librarian recorded the loan and told her the return date.
(f) Nila read the book carefully at home.
(g) The librarian checked the form and issued her a card.
(h) Nila then chose a storybook from a shelf.
items.explanation:
Correct order: c → b → a → g → h → e → f → d

Nila wanted to borrow a storybook from the town library. At the desk, the librarian explained that she needed a library card. Nila filled in the registration form with help from her parent. The librarian checked the form and issued her a card. Nila then chose a storybook from a shelf. The librarian recorded the loan and told her the return date. Nila read the book carefully at home. A week later, she returned it on time.

9. Put the following parts of the story in correct order to make the whole story. Write the corresponding letters in sequence.

(a) The authority later arranged for workers to repair the path.
(b) A group of neighbours noticed a broken path near their school.
(c) An official visited the site to inspect the problem.
(d) The gap made walking difficult, especially after rain.
(e) They photographed the damaged section without including anyone’s face.
(f) They thanked the workers and reminded everyone to report future damage.
(g) Next, they sent the location and photographs to the local authority.
(h) After the repair, the neighbours checked that the route was clear.
items.explanation:
Correct order: b → d → e → g → c → a → h → f

A group of neighbours noticed a broken path near their school. The gap made walking difficult, especially after rain. They photographed the damaged section without including anyone’s face. Next, they sent the location and photographs to the local authority. An official visited the site to inspect the problem. The authority later arranged for workers to repair the path. After the repair, the neighbours checked that the route was clear. They thanked the workers and reminded everyone to report future damage.

9. Put the following parts of the story in correct order to make the whole story. Write the corresponding letters in sequence.

(a) At the corner, they met a younger child who had lost sight of her guardian.
(b) One afternoon, a sudden shower began as Tuli left school.
(c) She had forgotten to bring her umbrella.
(d) Her friend Bithi saw her waiting beneath the school roof.
(e) Bithi offered to share her umbrella on the way home.
(f) They stayed with the child and informed a nearby teacher.
(g) After the teacher helped the child reunite with her guardian, the friends continued home.
(h) The two friends walked slowly to avoid the puddles.
items.explanation:
Correct order: b → c → d → e → h → a → f → g

One afternoon, a sudden shower began as Tuli left school. She had forgotten to bring her umbrella. Her friend Bithi saw her waiting beneath the school roof. Bithi offered to share her umbrella on the way home. The two friends walked slowly to avoid the puddles. At the corner, they met a younger child who had lost sight of her guardian. They stayed with the child and informed a nearby teacher. After the teacher helped the child reunite with her guardian, the friends continued home.

9. Put the following parts of the story in correct order to make the whole story. Write the corresponding letters in sequence.

(a) They planted vegetables and flowers in separate beds.
(b) The group created a schedule for watering the young plants.
(c) An unused plot beside a community centre had become covered with weeds.
(d) Several weeks later, the first vegetables were ready to pick.
(e) The neighbours shared the harvest and planned the next season.
(f) A group of neighbours asked permission to turn it into a garden.
(g) After permission was granted, they cleared the plot together.
(h) A gardener helped them choose plants suited to the site.
items.explanation:
Correct order: c → f → g → h → a → b → d → e

An unused plot beside a community centre had become covered with weeds. A group of neighbours asked permission to turn it into a garden. After permission was granted, they cleared the plot together. A gardener helped them choose plants suited to the site. They planted vegetables and flowers in separate beds. The group created a schedule for watering the young plants. Several weeks later, the first vegetables were ready to pick. The neighbours shared the harvest and planned the next season.

(a) We practised together and gave one another suggestions.
(b) Our teacher asked each group to prepare a short presentation.
(c) First, we listed the points we wanted to explain.
(d) Then we checked the information in reliable books.
(e) My group chose to speak about saving water.
(f) Each member prepared a small part of the talk.
(g) On presentation day, we spoke to the class and answered questions.
(h) The experience taught us the value of preparation and teamwork.
items.explanation:
Correct order: b → e → c → d → f → a → g → h

Our teacher asked each group to prepare a short presentation. My group chose to speak about saving water. First, we listed the points we wanted to explain. Then we checked the information in reliable books. Each member prepared a small part of the talk. We practised together and gave one another suggestions. On presentation day, we spoke to the class and answered questions. The experience taught us the value of preparation and teamwork.

9. Put the following parts of the story in correct order to make the whole story. Write the corresponding letters in sequence.

(a) The rescuer explained that young birds sometimes leave the nest before they can fly well.
(b) From a distance, she watched to see whether the bird was in immediate danger.
(c) She kept her cat indoors so it would not disturb the bird.
(d) She then asked an adult to contact a local wildlife rescuer for advice.
(e) Rina learned to seek expert advice instead of handling wildlife unnecessarily.
(f) Following the advice, the family kept people and pets away from the area.
(g) Later, they saw an adult bird return to feed the youngster.
(h) One morning, Rina saw a small bird on the ground near her home.
items.explanation:
Correct order: h → c → b → d → a → f → g → e

One morning, Rina saw a small bird on the ground near her home. She kept her cat indoors so it would not disturb the bird. From a distance, she watched to see whether the bird was in immediate danger. She then asked an adult to contact a local wildlife rescuer for advice. The rescuer explained that young birds sometimes leave the nest before they can fly well. Following the advice, the family kept people and pets away from the area. Later, they saw an adult bird return to feed the youngster. Rina learned to seek expert advice instead of handling wildlife unnecessarily.

9. Put the following parts of the story in correct order to make the whole story. Write the corresponding letters in sequence.

(a) They returned the books and recommended favourites to their friends.
(b) The teacher made a simple borrowing register.
(c) A teacher noticed that many children had few storybooks at home.
(d) Children began visiting the corner after school.
(e) Several families donated books that were clean and suitable for children.
(f) She spoke to neighbours about starting a small book corner.
(g) The project grew because everyone helped care for the collection.
(h) Volunteers placed the books on shelves in the community room.
items.explanation:
Correct order: c → f → e → h → b → d → a → g

A teacher noticed that many children had few storybooks at home. She spoke to neighbours about starting a small book corner. Several families donated books that were clean and suitable for children. Volunteers placed the books on shelves in the community room. The teacher made a simple borrowing register. Children began visiting the corner after school. They returned the books and recommended favourites to their friends. The project grew because everyone helped care for the collection.

9. Put the following parts of the story in correct order to make the whole story. Write the corresponding letters in sequence.

(a) Instead of throwing the bag away, she asked her aunt for help.
(b) The bag could hold her books again.
(c) Her aunt showed her how to thread a needle safely.
(d) Together they stitched along the torn edge.
(e) Sadia felt pleased that a simple repair had saved a useful object.
(f) Sadia found a small tear in her cloth bag.
(g) She repaired that part with her aunt’s guidance.
(h) Sadia examined the stitches and noticed a loose section.
items.explanation:
Correct order: f → a → c → d → h → g → b → e

Sadia found a small tear in her cloth bag. Instead of throwing the bag away, she asked her aunt for help. Her aunt showed her how to thread a needle safely. Together they stitched along the torn edge. Sadia examined the stitches and noticed a loose section. She repaired that part with her aunt’s guidance. The bag could hold her books again. Sadia felt pleased that a simple repair had saved a useful object.

9. Put the following parts of the story in correct order to make the whole story. Write the corresponding letters in sequence.

(a) On Thursday, interested students arrived at the correct room.
(b) The teacher noticed that the room number was missing.
(c) The secretary added the number to the notice.
(d) She then placed it on the school noticeboard.
(e) The school debate club decided to hold a meeting on Thursday.
(f) Its secretary wrote a notice with the date, time and place.
(g) Before displaying it, she asked the teacher to check the details.
(h) The meeting began on time because everyone had the necessary information.
items.explanation:
Correct order: e → f → g → b → c → d → a → h

The school debate club decided to hold a meeting on Thursday. Its secretary wrote a notice with the date, time and place. Before displaying it, she asked the teacher to check the details. The teacher noticed that the room number was missing. The secretary added the number to the notice. She then placed it on the school noticeboard. On Thursday, interested students arrived at the correct room. The meeting began on time because everyone had the necessary information.

9. Put the following parts of the story in correct order to make the whole story. Write the corresponding letters in sequence.

(a) His cousin appreciated the care Jamal had taken.
(b) He told his cousin rather than riding it immediately.
(c) Jamal borrowed his cousin’s bicycle for a short ride.
(d) They also tested the brakes before Jamal set out.
(e) He returned it to his cousin the same afternoon.
(f) After the ride, Jamal wiped the bicycle clean.
(g) Before leaving, he noticed that one tyre felt soft.
(h) Together they checked the tyre and added air.
items.explanation:
Correct order: c → g → b → h → d → f → e → a

Jamal borrowed his cousin’s bicycle for a short ride. Before leaving, he noticed that one tyre felt soft. He told his cousin rather than riding it immediately. Together they checked the tyre and added air. They also tested the brakes before Jamal set out. After the ride, Jamal wiped the bicycle clean. He returned it to his cousin the same afternoon. His cousin appreciated the care Jamal had taken.

9. Put the following parts of the story in correct order to make the whole story. Write the corresponding letters in sequence.

(a) The merchant sold him to a rich man in another country.
(b) To escape torture, he one day fled from his master's house.
(c) Once there lived a young man named Androcles.
(d) Unfortunately, he was caught by a slave merchant.
(e) He took shelter in a cave.
(f) He used to inflict heavy torture on him.
(g) It was unbearable for him.
(h) The man was very rude and cruel.
items.explanation:
Correct order: c → d → a → h → f → g → b → e

Once there lived a young man named Androcles. Unfortunately, he was caught by a slave merchant. The merchant sold him to a rich man in another country. The man was very rude and cruel. He used to inflict heavy torture on him. It was unbearable for him. To escape torture, he one day fled from his master's house. He took shelter in a cave.
